title: Kenora police need cultural training: jury
article: An inquest jury looking into the police shooting of a 17-year-old aboriginal youth ruled Friday that provincial police need cultural awareness training.

The five-member jury wrapped up its two-week examination into the death of Geronimo Fobister, who was killed on the Grassy Narrows First Nation in a confrontation with an Ontario Provincial Police emergency response unit last year.

Investigators said Fobister threatened police with a shotgun when officers tried to arrest him for a shooting earlier in the day. The jury ruled Fobister's death a homicide and presented 20 recommendations. Most were directed at police and include a call for mandatory aboriginal cultural awareness training for officers.
